name: addDockerHost
description: Creates a new docker daemon connection. For a unix socket use dockerType="socket" and dockerDaemon="/var/run/docker.sock". For a TCP proxy (e.g. tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy) use dockerType="tcp" and dockerDaemon="http://host:2375". Consider calling testDockerHost first to verify reachability.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Human-readable name for this docker host

arguments.name: dockerType
arguments.desc: "socket" for a unix socket path, "tcp" for an HTTP/HTTPS URL

arguments.name: dockerDaemon
arguments.desc: Unix socket path (e.g. /var/run/docker.sock) when dockerType=socket, or TCP URL (e.g. http://docker-proxy:2375) when dockerType=tcp

name: addNotification
description: Creates a new notification channel. The configuration fields depend on the notification type (e.g., for slack: webhookURL; for ntfy: ntfyTopic, ntfyServerUrl; for discord: discordWebhookUrl).

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Human-readable name for this notification channel

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Notification type (e.g. slack, ntfy, discord, telegram, webhook, smtp)

arguments.name: isDefault
arguments.desc: Enable by default for new monitors

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Apply this notification to all existing monitors now

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: Type-specific configuration fields (e.g. webhookURL for slack, ntfyTopic for ntfy)

name: addTag
description: Creates a new tag that can be assigned to monitors.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Tag name

arguments.name: color
arguments.desc: Tag color as a hex string (e.g. "#ff0000") or CSS color name

name: createMaintenance
description: Schedules a new maintenance window. During maintenance, the monitors in monitorIDs are suppressed and show MAINTENANCE status instead of DOWN. A window created without monitorIDs suppresses nothing. Use strategy "manual" for a window you switch on and off with resumeMaintenance / pauseMaintenance.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Title of the maintenance window

arguments.name: strategy
arguments.desc: Scheduling strategy: single=one-time, recurring-interval=every N days, recurring-weekday=specific weekdays, recurring-day-of-month=specific dates, cron=starts on a cron expression and lasts durationMinutes, manual=on whenever active

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Whether the window is active (default: true). For a manual window, active means in maintenance right now.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Description or reason for the maintenance

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.desc: Timezone the dates and times are in (e.g. "America/New_York", "UTC"). Omit to follow the server timezone.

arguments.name: dateRange
arguments.desc: [start, end] as local wall-clock times in the window's timezone, e.g. ["2026-10-08T10:00", "2026-10-08T12:00"] — the format Uptime Kuma's own UI stores. Required for single; optional bounds for recurring strategies; ignored for manual.

arguments.name: timeRange
arguments.desc: Daily [{hours, minutes}, {hours, minutes}] start and end. Required for the recurring-* strategies, ignored otherwise.

arguments.name: weekdays
arguments.desc: Days of week (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday) for recurring-weekday strategy

arguments.name: daysOfMonth
arguments.desc: Days of month (1-31) for recurring-day-of-month strategy

arguments.name: intervalDay
arguments.desc: Interval in days for recurring-interval strategy

arguments.name: cron
arguments.desc: Cron expression for when the window starts, e.g. "30 3 * * *" (03:30 daily), for the cron strategy

arguments.name: durationMinutes
arguments.desc: How long each window lasts, in minutes, for the cron strategy

arguments.name: monitorIDs
arguments.desc: IDs of the monitors this window suppresses. A window with no monitors suppresses nothing. On update this REPLACES the current list; pass [] to detach all.

name: createMonitor
description: Creates a new monitor in Uptime Kuma. Requires at minimum a name and type. Use listMonitorTypes to see supported types; prefer one made for the service (e.g. gamedig for a game server) over a port check. For HTTP monitors include url; for TCP/port monitors include hostname and port; for ping and dns include hostname; for json-query include url, jsonPath, jsonPathOperator and expectedValue; for database types (mysql, postgres, mongodb, redis, sqlserver, oracledb) include databaseConnectionString. For any other type, and for anything type-specific such as HTTP authentication, call getMonitorTypeFields first: it lists the required and optional fields of the type, what each means, and whether it is passed at the top level or inside typeFields. A create without the required fields of its type is refused rather than saved as a monitor that fails every check. For an HTTP monitor behind authentication pass the credentials in typeFields (basic_auth_user and basic_auth_pass, or bearer_token) and authMethod is set to match. Never pass "***" for a credential. A push monitor is given a generated push token (Uptime Kuma only generates one in its own web UI) and the resulting ping URL is returned. Omitted settings get the web form's defaults: interval 60 (300 for ntp), retryInterval equal to interval, and a per-type timeout.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Display name for the monitor

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Monitor type (e.g. http, port, ping, dns, push, keyword). Use listMonitorTypes for all options.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Free-text description shown on the monitor page

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Whether the monitor starts checking immediately (default: true). Pass false to create it paused.

arguments.name: resendInterval
arguments.desc: Resend notification every N checks while down (0 = disabled, the default)

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.desc: Request timeout in SECONDS. Omit for the web form's default: 48, or 10 for ping, 5 for snmp and 1 for kafka-producer, at most 0.8 x interval. Avoid 0: Uptime Kuma's runtime fallback for a stored 0 computes interval * 1000 * 0.8 and then multiplies by 1000 again, yielding a ~13 hour timeout, so the monitor can never report DOWN against a host that accepts the connection and never answers. Push and group monitors do not use it; a 0 stored on one of those is harmless.

arguments.name: jsonPath
arguments.desc: JSONata expression for json-query monitors. Must resolve to a primitive.

arguments.name: jsonPathOperator
arguments.desc: Comparison operator for json-query monitors. UP while value <operator> expectedValue.

arguments.name: expectedValue
arguments.desc: Threshold the json-query result is compared against. Stored as a string.

arguments.name: pushToken
arguments.desc: Push token for push monitors — the secret in the ping URL. Omit and one is generated and returned.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: URL to monitor (required for http, keyword and json-query; other types that need it are listed by getMonitorTypeFields)

arguments.name: hostname
arguments.desc: Hostname or IP address to check (required for port, ping and dns, and most non-HTTP types — see getMonitorTypeFields)

arguments.name: port
arguments.desc: Port number (required for port; see getMonitorTypeFields for other types)

arguments.name: interval
arguments.desc: Check interval in seconds (default: 60, or 300 for ntp; min: 1)

arguments.name: retryInterval
arguments.desc: Retry interval in seconds when monitor is down (default: the interval, min: 1)

arguments.name: maxretries
arguments.desc: Max retries before marking as down (default: 0)

arguments.name: notificationIDList
arguments.desc: Map of notification IDs to enable (e.g. {"1": true, "3": true})

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tags to assign to the monitor

arguments.name: keyword
arguments.desc: Keyword to search for (keyword monitor type)

arguments.name: invertKeyword
arguments.desc: Invert keyword match

arguments.name: method
arguments.desc: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) for http type

arguments.name: body
arguments.desc: HTTP request body

arguments.name: headers
arguments.desc: HTTP headers as JSON string

arguments.name: accepted_statuscodes
arguments.desc: Accepted HTTP status codes (e.g. ["200-299"])

arguments.name: ignoreTls
arguments.desc: Ignore TLS/SSL errors

arguments.name: maxredirects
arguments.desc: Max HTTP redirects (default: 10)

arguments.name: upsideDown
arguments.desc: Invert status — treat up as down

arguments.name: expiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the TLS certificate expires (http, keyword, json-query, globalping)

arguments.name: domainExpiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the domain registration expires (most types with a url or hostname; see getMonitorTypeFields). Needs Uptime Kuma 2.1 or later.

arguments.name: parent
arguments.desc: Parent group monitor ID

arguments.name: docker_container
arguments.desc: Docker container name (required for docker type)

arguments.name: docker_host
arguments.desc: Docker host ID (required for docker type). Use listDockerHosts to find available IDs.

arguments.name: dns_resolve_server
arguments.desc: DNS server to use for resolution (required for dns type, default: 1.1.1.1)

arguments.name: dns_resolve_type
arguments.desc: DNS record type to query, for dns and globalping (default: A). Which types each supports: getMonitorTypeFields

arguments.name: databaseConnectionString
arguments.desc: Connection string for mysql, postgres, mongodb, redis, sqlserver and oracledb monitors (required for those types). For oracledb the login goes in basic_auth_user and basic_auth_pass. A credential: read tools return it as "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: databaseQuery
arguments.desc: Query for database monitors. SQL for mysql, postgres and sqlserver (default: SELECT 1) and oracledb (default: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL); a JSON command object for mongodb (default: {"ping": 1}).

arguments.name: databasePassword
arguments.desc: Password for mysql monitors, if not inline in the connection string. Stored by Uptime Kuma as radiusPassword. A credential: read tools return it as "***".

arguments.name: radiusPassword
arguments.desc: The RADIUS password (required for radius). Also the column databasePassword and typeFields.snmpCommunity are stored in — prefer those names for mysql and snmp.

arguments.name: typeFields
arguments.desc: Fields specific to the monitor type, e.g. {"mqttTopic": "sensors/#"} for mqtt or {"bearer_token": "…"} for an HTTP monitor behind authentication. Call getMonitorTypeFields with the type for the names, meanings and allowed values — they are validated, and an unknown name is refused. getMonitor returns these fields at the top level of the monitor; to change one, pass it here.

name: createStatusPage
description: Creates a new (empty) status page with the given title and slug. After creating, call updateStatusPage to set the description, theme, groups, and monitors. Slug must be lowercase letters, digits, and dashes only.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Display title of the status page

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: URL slug (lowercase letters, digits, and dashes only)

name: deleteDockerHost
description: Permanently deletes a docker daemon connection. Any monitors referencing it will have their docker_host cleared by Uptime Kuma (the monitors themselves are not deleted).

arguments.name: dockerHostID
arguments.desc: The ID of the docker host to delete

name: deleteMaintenance
description: Permanently deletes a maintenance window. Its monitors return to normal alerting. Use getMaintenanceWindows to find the ID.

arguments.name: maintenanceID
arguments.desc: The ID of the maintenance window to delete

name: deleteMonitor
description: Permanently deletes a monitor and all its heartbeat history. This action cannot be undone.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to delete

name: deleteNotification
description: Permanently deletes a notification channel. Monitors that used this channel will no longer send alerts through it.

arguments.name: notificationID
arguments.desc: The ID of the notification to delete

name: deleteStatusPage
description: Permanently deletes a status page by slug. The status page URL will no longer be accessible.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug to delete

name: deleteTag
description: Permanently deletes a tag. It will be removed from all monitors that use it. Use listTags to find the tag ID.

arguments.name: tagID
arguments.desc: The ID of the tag to delete

name: getHeartbeats
description: Retrieves historical heartbeat data for a specific monitor (response times, status changes over time). Use this for analyzing patterns or history for one monitor. Beats are returned NEWEST-FIRST. By default returns only the most recent heartbeat; set maxHeartbeats (up to 100) for historical analysis. Keep maxHeartbeats ≤10 unless user requests more. Set important:true for the status CHANGES only (Uptime Kuma's own event list) — that is history, not current state, so do not read status from it. Credentials embedded in a status message URL (user:pass@host) read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to get heartbeats for

arguments.name: maxHeartbeats
arguments.desc: If set, returns the most recent X heartbeats (up to 100). If unset, returns only the most recent heartbeat (default: 1)

arguments.name: important
arguments.desc: Return only IMPORTANT beats — the status changes behind Uptime Kuma's event list — fetched live from the server rather than the cache. History only: the newest important beat is not the monitor's current status.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: getMaintenanceWindows
description: Returns all maintenance windows defined in Uptime Kuma, each with monitorIDs — the monitors it suppresses. A window with an empty monitorIDs list suppresses nothing.

name: getMonitor
description: Retrieves configuration details for a specific monitor by ID (URL, check interval, notification settings, etc.). Use this when you need to examine or modify settings for a specific monitor. For current status, use getMonitorSummary instead. By default returns only common fields plus runtime data (uptime, avgPing); set includeTypeSpecificFields to true to include type-specific fields (e.g., url for HTTP, hostname/port for TCP).

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to retrieve

arguments.name: includeTypeSpecificFields
arguments.desc: Include type-specific fields (url, hostname, port, etc.) in addition to common fields. Default: false. When false, only returns MonitorBase fields plus uptime/avgPing.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: getMonitorSummary
description: START HERE for status overview questions. Retrieves current status for all monitors showing UP/DOWN/PENDING/MAINTENANCE states with the most recent heartbeat message. Use this when asked "how is everything doing?", "what's down?", "what's up?", or for any general status overview. Returns essential information (ID, name, pathName, active state, maintenance state, status, message, lastBeatTime, type, tags). Supports filtering by keywords, type, active/maintenance status, tags, parent group, and current status. Check lastBeatTime before trusting the status of a push monitor — one that has stopped beating keeps reporting its last known status. lastBeatTime is UTC with no zone marker, so measure staleness against the current UTC time.

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Space-separated keywords to filter monitors by pathName (case-insensitive fuzzy match). All keywords must match for a monitor to be included.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Filter by monitor type(s). Comma-separated for multiple types. Use listMonitorTypes tool to see all available types.

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Filter by active status. true=only active monitors, false=only inactive monitors.

arguments.name: maintenance
arguments.desc: Filter by maintenance status. true=only monitors in maintenance, false=only monitors not in maintenance.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Filter by tag name and optional value. Comma-separated for multiple tags. Format: "tagName" or "tagName=value". Monitor must have all specified tags. Case-insensitive. Examples: "production", "env=staging", "production,region=us-east"

arguments.name: parentId
arguments.desc: Filter to the DIRECT children of this group monitor. Pass null for top-level monitors (those with no parent). Not recursive — use the group's own childrenIDs to walk deeper.

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: Filter by current heartbeat status. Comma-separated for multiple statuses. 0=DOWN, 1=UP, 2=PENDING, 3=MAINTENANCE. Examples: "0", "1", "0,2"

name: getMonitorTypeFields
description: Describes the fields one monitor type uses: which are required, which are optional, what each means and accepts, and the defaults applied when they are omitted. Call this before createMonitor, or before updateMonitor changes a type or sets type-specific fields: most of them go in the typeFields argument of those tools, which is not described there.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: The monitor type, e.g. http, mqtt, snmp. Use listMonitorTypes for all options.

name: getSettings
description: Retrieves the current Uptime Kuma server settings, such as timezone, primary base URL and data retention. Uptime Kuma only returns settings that have been saved, so a setting missing from the result (for example primaryBaseURL) has never been set.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: getStatusPage
description: Returns the full configuration of a status page by slug, including the ordered list of groups, the monitors inside each group, and active incidents. Works for unpublished pages too.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug (the URL-safe identifier)

name: listDockerHosts
description: Returns all docker daemon connections configured in Uptime Kuma. These are referenced by docker container monitors via docker_host.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: listHeartbeats
description: Retrieves historical heartbeat data for ALL monitors (response times, status changes over time). Use this for analyzing patterns across multiple monitors or correlating events. Beats are returned NEWEST-FIRST. By default returns only the most recent heartbeat per monitor; set maxHeartbeats (up to 100) for historical analysis. Keep maxHeartbeats ≤5 unless user requests more. Credentials embedded in a status message URL (user:pass@host) read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: maxHeartbeats
arguments.desc: If set, returns the most recent X heartbeats per monitor (up to 100). If unset, returns only the most recent heartbeat per monitor (default: 1)

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: listMonitors
description: Retrieves configuration details for all monitors (URLs, check intervals, notification settings, etc.). Use this when you need to examine or modify monitor settings. For status checks ("how is everything doing?", "what's down?"), use getMonitorSummary instead. By default returns only common fields plus runtime data (uptime, avgPing); set includeTypeSpecificFields to true to include type-specific fields (e.g., url for HTTP, hostname/port for TCP). Supports filtering by keywords, type, active/maintenance status, tags, and parent group.

arguments.name: includeTypeSpecificFields
arguments.desc: Include type-specific fields (url, hostname, port, etc.) in addition to common fields. Default: false. When false, only returns MonitorBase fields plus uptime/avgPing.

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Space-separated keywords to filter monitors by pathName (case-insensitive fuzzy match). All keywords must match for a monitor to be included.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Filter by monitor type(s). Comma-separated for multiple types. Use listMonitorTypes tool to see all available types.

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Filter by active status. true=only active monitors, false=only inactive monitors.

arguments.name: maintenance
arguments.desc: Filter by maintenance status. true=only monitors in maintenance, false=only monitors not in maintenance.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Filter by tag name and optional value. Comma-separated for multiple tags. Format: "tagName" or "tagName=value". Monitor must have all specified tags. Case-insensitive. Examples: "production", "env=staging", "production,region=us-east"

arguments.name: parentId
arguments.desc: Filter to the DIRECT children of this group monitor. Pass null for top-level monitors (those with no parent). Not recursive — use the group's own childrenIDs to walk deeper.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: listMonitorTypes
description: Returns every monitor type Uptime Kuma supports, with what each one checks. Use it to choose the type for createMonitor — there are dedicated types for game servers, MQTT, RADIUS, SNMP, SMTP, gRPC, Docker containers and more — and to find valid values for type filters in other tools.

name: listNotifications
description: Returns all configured notification channels (Slack, ntfy, Discord, email, webhooks, etc.), each with its `type` and its type-specific settings in `config`. To attach a channel to a monitor you only need its id — the credentials in `config` are withheld by default and the names of the withheld fields are listed in `redactedConfigKeys`.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***". Off by default: this output is persisted in conversation transcripts and logs. Can also be enabled globally with UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS=true.

name: listStatusPages
description: Returns all configured status pages with their slug, title, visibility, and custom domain settings. Uptime Kuma only sends this list when a client logs in, so a page created or deleted by another client (or the web UI) since then may be missing or still listed; changes made through this server are reflected at once. getStatusPage with a slug always reads the page fresh.

name: listTags
description: Returns all tags defined in Uptime Kuma (name, color, and ID).

name: pauseMaintenance
description: Switches a maintenance window off: it stops suppressing its monitors and its schedule stops until resumed. For a manual window this ends the maintenance.

arguments.name: maintenanceID
arguments.desc: The ID of the maintenance window to pause

name: resumeMaintenance

arguments.name: monitorID

name: updateMonitor
description: Updates an existing monitor configuration. You must include the monitorID. Only the fields you provide will be changed (the server merges your changes with the existing config). Use getMonitor first to get the current config. Passing a different type converts the monitor in place, keeping its ID and history: the new type must have the fields it needs, passed here or already stored (e.g. url for http, hostname for ping), and a monitor becoming push is given a push token if it has none. Type-specific fields go in typeFields; call getMonitorTypeFields for their names and meanings. Credentials read back as "***"; sending "***" keeps the stored value.

arguments.name: databaseQuery
arguments.desc: Query for database monitors. SQL for mysql, postgres, sqlserver and oracledb; a JSON command object for mongodb.

arguments.name: databasePassword
arguments.desc: Password for mysql monitors, stored by Uptime Kuma as radiusPassword. Sending "***" back keeps the stored value.

arguments.name: radiusPassword
arguments.desc: The RADIUS password (required for radius). Also the column databasePassword and typeFields.snmpCommunity are stored in — prefer those names for mysql and snmp.

arguments.name: typeFields
arguments.desc: Fields specific to the monitor type, e.g. {"mqttTopic": "sensors/#"} for mqtt or {"bearer_token": "…"} for an HTTP monitor behind authentication. Call getMonitorTypeFields with the type for the names, meanings and allowed values — they are validated, and an unknown name is refused. getMonitor returns these fields at the top level of the monitor; to change one, pass it here.

name: updateNotification
description: Updates an existing notification channel. Use listNotifications to find the notification ID.

arguments.name: notificationID
arguments.desc: The ID of the notification to update

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Human-readable name

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Notification type

arguments.name: isDefault
arguments.desc: Enable by default for new monitors

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Apply to all existing monitors now

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: Type-specific configuration fields to update

name: updateStatusPage
description: Updates an existing status page. config holds only the settings to change; everything else keeps its stored value. publicGroupList, when given, replaces all of the page's groups (a group not in it is deleted; include a group's id to keep it rather than recreate it); omit it to keep the groups as they are. Each group has a name and a monitorList of [{id}]. Use getStatusPage first to read current state before modifying.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug (immutable identifier)

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: The settings to change, merged onto the stored page: title, description, theme, published, showTags, showPoweredBy, domainNameList, customCSS, footerText, icon, etc. Omit to change only the groups.

arguments.name: publicGroupList
arguments.desc: Ordered groups, replacing all current ones. Each: {id?, name, monitorList: [{id}]}. Omit to keep the current groups.

arguments.name: imgDataUrl
arguments.desc: Icon as data URL. Omit or pass empty string to keep existing.
